Fit a SITAR growth curve model safely

Source: R/curve-sitar.R
wgh_fit_sitar.Rd

Fits a SuperImposition by Translation And Rotation model with sitar::sitar(), keeping every warning and returning NULL with the error message rather than stopping, so competing specifications can be compared (as fit_sitar_safe() did in the analysis code of Ho et al. 2026, medRxiv 2026.07.26.26358986). Diagnostics are attached.

Usage

wgh_fit_sitar(
  x,
  df = wgh_opt("sitar_df"),
  fixed = "a + b + c",
  random = "a + b + c",
  age_range = c(6, 18),
  min_visits = 3,
  sex = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  max_iter = 200,
  retry = TRUE,
  max_children = wgh_opt("subsample"),
  seed = 2026,
  max_time = 900
)

Arguments

x

Growth data with id (or pid), age and height.

df

Degrees of freedom of the mean spline.

fixed, random

SITAR fixed and random effects, "a + b + c" or "a + b + c + d".

age_range

Ages to include.

min_visits

Minimum visits per child.

sex

Optional sex to restrict to.

label

Label used in tables.

max_iter

Maximum iterations of the optimiser.

retry

If the fit fails, retry once with one fewer degree of freedom.

max_children

Largest number of children used. SITAR fits on tens of thousands of children take hours, so by default the run mode sets the limit (1,000 children in "dev", 10,000 in "analysis" and all children in "publication"). Use Inf for all children.

seed

Random seed for choosing the children. The caller's random stream is restored.

max_time

Longest fitting time in seconds. A model that does not converge in that time is stopped and returned as a failed fit with the reason, so a model comparison or flow never hangs. Inf for no limit.

Value

An object of class wgh_sitar with model (the sitar fit or NULL), warnings, label, data and the fitting settings.

Examples

# \donttest{
boys <- growdat2_mini[growdat2_mini$sex == "Male", ]
fit <- wgh_fit_sitar(boys, df = 4, age_range = c(6, 18))
fit
